sights.n: Arakaki Family Residence, Tsuboya (新垣家住宅)
sights.w: The only surviving 18th-century Tsuboya potter's compound — red-tiled main house, workshop, climbing kiln (the former royal 'Higashi-nu-kama') and stone pigsty-toilet — designated an Important Cultural Property in 2002.
sights.k: Important Cultural Property · Tsuboya potter's house & climbing kiln

sights.n: Tsushima Maru Memorial Museum (対馬丸記念館)
sights.w: Museum (opened 22 Aug 2004) on the 1944 sinking of the evacuation ship Tsushima Maru, in which hundreds of Okinawan schoolchildren died; run by the Tsushima Maru Memorial Association beside Gokoku-ji and Naminoue.

sights.n: Mekaru Tomb Site, Shintoshin (銘苅墓跡群)
sights.address: Mekaru 2-chōme (hill opposite the Naha City Fire Department HQ), Naha, Okinawa
sights.w: National Historic Site (2007): a hillside necropolis of 330+ tombs spanning the Gusuku era through the Ryūkyū Kingdom to Meiji, the oldest from the 14th–15th c.; its largest turtleback tomb is 22 m wide and 30 m deep. Survived the build-out of Naha Shintoshin.
sights.k: National Historic Site · 330 Ryūkyū tombs in the new city centre

sights.w: Shingon temple founded in 1367 beside Naminoue Shrine, once the Ryūkyū Kingdom's royal prayer temple and head of Shingon in the kingdom. Missionary Bernard Bettelheim occupied it 1846–1853, and its 1465 bell was given to Commodore Perry (long kept at Annapolis).
sights.k: Ryūkyū royal temple · Bettelheim & Perry's bell
